newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds maintained some of their early gains by the close after a shaky session during which they reacted along with other Euro markets to the European Commission's forecasts and comments over EMU.
"Bonos are still looking for a new fair value after yesterday's fast rise," said Fernando Mena, dealer at Fimat.
He said strong resistance was seen around 109.50, just where the futures contract reached its record high this morning.
The European Commission said it would be watching to see that Madrid met its 4.4 percent public budget deficit over GDP forecast for 1996.
The 10-year spread over Bunds remained at 162 basis points, while the differential over Btps was at 28 bps at the close.
A possible fast re-entry of the lira into the Erm should favor Bonos too, dealers said.

Earlier Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Ciampi said Italy was likely to seek lira re-entry by end November. "Foreign investors took long positions trying to anticipate that move," said an economist. "And so when they will be really back again it is very likely we will see profit taking on Btps".
